Make the most of your 30 seconds.
Start by finding one answer you trust. T: Start by finding one answer you trust. Then look for a less obvious answer that still fits every part of the prompt. These rare-answer trivia tips help you decide when to take that chance during RARE Air's five-question flights.
Read the boundary before searching your: Read the boundary before searching your memory.
Watch for a named edition, a date range,: Watch for a named edition, a date range, a starting letter or a particular region. A correct answer to the general topic can fall outside a narrower prompt. For example, membership of a specific fictional group is different from appearing anywhere in the same story.
Use the opening seconds to identify the: Use the opening seconds to identify the exact set of things the question accepts. That makes the rest of your recall more focused.
Keep a dependable answer in reserve.
Recall a familiar example first. If anot: Recall a familiar example first. If another answer comes to mind, check that it belongs to the same set before submitting. Correctness earns altitude at every tier, so an unfamiliar guess needs to justify the risk of scoring zero.
Avoid spending the whole clock searching: Avoid spending the whole clock searching for a perfect answer. RARE Air gives you 30 seconds for an active prompt. The server keeps that clock running while you switch tabs or open a dialog.
Search a category in smaller groups.
If a broad category feels blank, try men: If a broad category feels blank, try mentally grouping it by place, period or subject. For a geography prompt, move through regions. For a literature prompt, recall authors or series you know. This is a recall technique, so every candidate still needs to satisfy the actual question.
Use the ordinary name when you know it. RARE Air normalizes capitalization, punctuation and accepted aliases. A spelling variation works when it is present in the curated answer list.
Use the pauses and the flight report.
The reward screen waits for you to press: The reward screen waits for you to press Climb higher. Take a breath there. The next question stays hidden during the pause, then a three-second preparation countdown introduces the next stage.
At the end, review the accepted answers: At the end, review the accepted answers and their editorial tiers. Choose one or two unfamiliar answers to remember, and look up the topic if you want more context. Practice flights provide another five prompts without changing the shared daily leaderboard.
Treat tiers as the game's scoring rules.
RARE Air uses fixed editorial rarity tie: RARE Air uses fixed editorial rarity tiers, so choosing an answer that feels obscure does not guarantee the maximum score. Your completed report shows how that answer was rated. A missing valid answer can be reported to the maintainer with a reliable source and the prompt's exact wording.
